sentences.en: A spectre is haunting Europe, the spectre of communism.
sentences.zh: 一个幽灵，共产主义的幽灵，在欧洲游荡。

sentences.en: All the powers of old Europe have entered into a holy alliance to exorcise this spectre.
sentences.zh: 旧欧洲的一切势力，都为驱除这个幽灵而结成了神圣同盟。

sentences.en: So begins the Communist Manifesto, written in 1848 by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
sentences.zh: 《共产党宣言》就这样开篇了，它由卡尔·马克思和弗里德里希·恩格斯于1848年撰写。

sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History with me, Dominic Sandbrook, well-known Marxist, and my sidekick, wishy-washy, Brixton, centrist liberal Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史其余部分》，我是多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，一名知名的马克思主义者，旁边这位是我的搭档、优柔寡断的布里克斯顿中产阶级自由派汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: Hello, comrade.
sentences.zh: 你好，同志。

sentences.en: Hello, comrade.
sentences.zh: 你好，同志。

sentences.en: So today we're talking about communism, the great political theory that dominated so much conversation in the late 19th and much of the 20th centuries.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天要聊聊共产主义，这个在19世纪末和20世纪大部分时间里主导了无数对话的伟大政治理论。

sentences.en: And actually, looking back, Tom, when we were kids, communism and capitalism were locked in this genuine competition, so it seemed, for the hearts and minds of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 事实上，回过头来看，汤姆，在我们小的时候，共产主义和资本主义似乎正卷入一场真正的竞争，争夺数百万人的心智。

sentences.en: I mean, when you survey the world, the map, I can remember those maps from my kind of childhood.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你审视这个世界、这张地图时，我还记得我童年时看到的那些地图。

sentences.en: You had the Soviet Union and all its satellite states, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, Poland,
sentences.zh: 当时有苏联及其所有卫星国，捷克斯洛伐克、南斯拉夫、波兰，

sentences.en: Hungary, East Germany, and so on.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利、东德等等。

sentences.en: You had, in Africa, you had places like Angola, Ethiopia, Mozambique.
sentences.zh: 在非洲，有安哥拉、埃塞俄比亚、莫桑比克这样的地方。

sentences.en: You had Afghanistan, Mongolia, of course, the People's Republic of China, which is still technically communist, as are Cuba, Vietnam, and Laos.
sentences.zh: 还有阿富汗、蒙古，当然，还有中华人民共和国，从名义上讲它至今仍是共产主义国家，古巴、越南和老挝也是如此。

sentences.en: But there's been a huge falling off since then.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，共产主义的影响力大幅下降了。

sentences.en: So do you think communism is gone, or is it still with us?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得共产主义已经消亡了，还是依然存在于我们身边？

sentences.en: I think it's such a potent idea, and it won't surprise you to know why I think it's a potent idea.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个极具潜力的思想，而且你知道我认为它潜力巨大的原因，也一定不会感到意外。

sentences.en: I can't wait for this.
sentences.zh: 我已经迫不及待了。

sentences.en: I think it has very, very deep roots, and maybe we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 我认为它有着非常非常深厚的根基，也许我们待会儿会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: And I think that the guiding kind of ideal that it embodies, that all of humanity can be liberated, and that all of humanity can share in an equal justice, is one that has
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它所体现的核心理想——全人类都可以得到解放，全人类都可以共享平等的正义——这种理想具有

sentences.en: an obvious appeal.
sentences.zh: 一种显而易见的吸引力。

sentences.en: And I guess that when we talk about communism, we tend to mean the specific form that it has taken in the writings of Marx, and then the way that it's evolved with Lenin and with
sentences.zh: 我想，当我们谈论共产主义时，我们往往指的是它在马克思著作中所呈现的具体形式，以及后来通过列宁和

sentences.en: Mao, and through the ideological war of the 20th century, as you said.
sentences.zh: 毛泽东演变而来的形式，并如你所说，通过20世纪的意识形态战争延续下来的形式。

sentences.en: But I do absolutely think that, I mean, it's, you know, China, potentially the greatest power on the face of the planet, remains a communist state.
sentences.zh: 但我绝对认为，中国，这个潜在的地球上最强大的国家，依然是一个共产主义国家。

sentences.en: So it's ridiculous to say that, you know, communism has gone the way of Nineveh and Tyre, simply purely on the political level.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果仅仅从政治层面，就断言共产主义已经像尼尼微和推罗一样消亡了，那是极其荒谬的。

sentences.en: But I think it also has, continues to have a huge influence on the cultural level.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它在文化层面也继续产生着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So I would say that probably the two most influential communist thinkers at the moment would be Antonia Gramsci, Italian, writing in the 30s, who argued that essentially kind
sentences.zh: 所以如果要说，当今最具影响力的两位马克思主义思想家，可能会是安东尼奥·葛兰西，这位在30年代写作的意大利人，他认为本质上

sentences.en: of culture is the way for social justice to be established.
sentences.zh: 文化是建立社会正义的途径。

sentences.en: And that's been hugely influential in all kinds of ways that people understand the operation of culture.
sentences.zh: 这种观点在人们理解文化运作的各种方式上产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And I'd say Frans Fanon, the great Martinique francophone writer who has essentially kind of
sentences.zh: 还有弗朗茨·法农，这位伟大的马提尼克法语作家，他本质上将

sentences.en: articulated a Marxist understanding of world politics with an emphasis on how colonized societies
sentences.zh: 马克思主义对世界政治的理解阐述出来，重点关注被殖民社会

sentences.en: and the global South can fight back against what he casts as oppressive imperial domination.
sentences.zh: 和全球南方如何反抗他所描述的压迫性帝国统治。

sentences.en: And I would say that both of those thinkers have an, you know, colossal influence.
sentences.zh: 我认为这两位思想家都产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, I go so far as to say that actually, in a way, you could say that Marxism is more influential at the moment in the United States than it is in China.
sentences.zh: 我甚至想说，从某种程度上讲，马克思主义当今在美国的影响力其实比在中国还要大。

sentences.en: Discuss.
sentences.zh: 请大家讨论一下。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有意思。

sentences.en: That's an interesting argument.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的论点。

sentences.en: But they're both offshoots, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但它们都是分支，不是吗？

sentences.en: From the sort of the main trunk of communism, which we associate with Marxism.
sentences.zh: 源自我们与马克思主义联系在一起的共产主义主干。

sentences.en: So there had been ideas about a communist society before.
sentences.zh: 因此，在此之前就已经有过关于共产主义社会的思想了。

sentences.en: So Thomas More in his book, Utopia, at the beginning of the turn of the 16th century, has this vision of a society where people share property in an idealized sort of post-feudal
sentences.zh: 比如托马斯·莫尔在16世纪初的书《乌托邦》中，就构想了一种人们在理想化的后封建

sentences.en: world and the diggers in the English Civil War.
sentences.zh: 世界中共享财产的社会，还有英国内战中的掘地派。

sentences.en: But I mean, these are communists of a kind.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这些也可以算是一种共产主义者。

sentences.en: They're kind of proto-Marxist ideas, you could argue, couldn't you?
sentences.zh: 可以说，它们是一种前马克思主义的思想，不是吗？

sentences.en: Can I?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.zh: 你想搬出你的书吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to do your thing?
sentences.zh: 你想老调重弹吗？

sentences.en: I mean, everybody's waiting for this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家都在等着呢。

sentences.en: I'm not going to mention my book, but I would say that the prototype of a communist society is the early church.
sentences.zh: 我不想提我的书，但我得说共产主义社会的雏形其实是早期教会。

sentences.en: I'm giving you a hard time, Tom, for no very good reason, because I actually find you very convincing on this.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我无缘无故地难为你，因为我其实觉得你在这个问题上非常有说服力。

sentences.en: I genuinely think you're onto something.
sentences.zh: 我真心觉得你切中要害了。

sentences.en: So go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以，请继续吧。

sentences.en: So I think the prototype is the description of the early church in the Acts of the Apostles,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得雏形就是《使徒行传》中对早期教会的描述，

sentences.en: where it says that the apostles selling their possessions and goods gave to anyone as he had need.
sentences.zh: 里面提到使徒们卖掉自己的财产和物品，照各人所需的分给各人。

sentences.en: And there's an obvious echo there of Marx's famous dictum, from each according to his ability to each according to his needs.
sentences.zh: 这显然呼应了马克思的那句名言：各尽所能，按需分配。

sentences.en: And essentially, that posed a kind of challenge to Christians, which is, is this a kind of realisable ideal?
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这对基督徒提出了一个挑战，那就是：这是一种可以实现的理想吗？

sentences.en: And it's hard to overemphasize the degree to which in the Roman world, the rich and the powerful assume themselves to be morally superior to those who are poor.
sentences.zh: 我们很难过于夸大在罗马世界中，富人和有权势者认为自己在道德上优于穷人的这种程度。

sentences.en: And Christianity represents a really profound challenge to that assumption.
sentences.zh: 而基督教对这种假设提出了非常深刻的挑战。

sentences.en: And in the fifth century, you start to get the notion of a kind of class war that is motivated by Christian doctrine.
sentences.zh: 到了五世纪，开始出现由基督教教义驱动的阶级战争的概念。

sentences.en: And there's actually a British thinker called Pelagius, who argues that humans can redeem themselves from sin through their own efforts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时有一位名叫伯拉纠的英国思想家，他认为人类可以通过自身的努力从罪恶中获得救赎。

sentences.en: And this manifests itself in a kind of particularly radical Pelagian thought, with the idea that
sentences.zh: 这表现为一种特别激进的伯拉纠主义思想，认为

sentences.en: the whole of history is an expression basically of the war of the rich on the poor.
sentences.zh: 整部历史基本上就是富人对穷人战争的表现。

sentences.en: And that therefore, if you get rid of the rich, then you will have paradise on earth.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你消灭了富人，你就能在人间建立乐园。

sentences.en: And this gets opposed by particularly Augustine, the great father of the church, who says that humanity has fallen.
sentences.zh: 这一观点遭到了特别是伟大教会之父奥古斯丁的反对，他指出人类已经堕落了。

sentences.en: We can't possibly realise heaven on earth.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不可能在人间实现天堂。

sentences.en: And so the best that can be hoped for is that the rich will continue to give to the poor.
sentences.zh: 所以人们能抱有的最大希望，就是富人会继续施舍给穷人。

sentences.en: And I think that in essence, I mean, you could say that there you have communism against social democracy set up in the fifth century Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 我想本质上，你可以说，早在五世纪的罗马帝国，你就已经看到了共产主义与社会民主主义的对立。

sentences.en: It's basically Karl Marx and the Cadbury's family, the sort of philanthropists of...
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是卡尔·马克思与吉百利家族的对立，也就是那些慈善家的...

sentences.en: Yes, essentially.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: ...is a chocolate magnate.
sentences.zh: ...巧克力大亨。

sentences.en: Essentially.
sentences.zh: 基本上是的。

sentences.en: And Augustine's influence is obviously, he's the huge influence on the church.
sentences.zh: 奥古斯丁的影响显然很大，他对教会产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Pelagius gets branded a heretic.
sentences.zh: 伯拉纠则被打上了异端的烙印。

sentences.en: And so over the course of the church's history, there's an extreme anxiety about any suggestion
sentences.zh: 因此，在教会历史的发展过程中，人们对任何将基督教教义（尤其是福音书中的教导——贫穷的人有福了，最后将成为最初，最初将成为最后）

sentences.en: that Christian teaching, particularly in the Gospels, you know, woe to the rich, the last shall be first and the first will be last, that these sayings of Christ should be put
sentences.zh: 付诸社会实践的建议都感到极度的焦虑。

sentences.en: into social practice.
sentences.zh: 付诸社会实践。

sentences.en: But you do start by the...
sentences.zh: 但你从...

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从本质上讲，激进边缘时期的宗教改革就是一次将其付诸实践的尝试。

sentences.en: Although, of course, you have Calvinists who think if you're rich and successful, that shows that God is smiling on you and that actually being a wealthy sort of merchant or
sentences.zh: 当然，加尔文主义者认为，如果你富有且成功，那就表明上帝在对你微笑，作为一个富有的商人或

sentences.zh: 但在非常非常激进的边缘群体中，甚至在宗教改革之前的胡斯

sentences.zh: 事实上，他杀害了这么多人，原因是他认为这是实现人间天堂的途径，他其实是个坚定的马克思主义者。

sentences.en: He spent all his life immersed in Marxist ideas.
sentences.zh: 这就是，你知道的，当他做出决定时，始终驱使着他的东西。

sentences.en: He's written tons of incredibly tedious articles about aspects of Marxism in Bolshevik journals.
sentences.zh: 事实上，暴力是内在的，杀戮也是内在的，因为这是实现这个美好社会的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And actually, the reason that he kills all these people is because he thinks that's the way to achieve the paradise, that he's actually a good MarxiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当你审视斯大林、毛泽东甚至是希特勒时，你必须记住，在他们的眼里，他们所做的一切都是为了至善。

sentences.en: And that's the thing that, you know, when he makes his decisions, that's what always drives him on.
sentences.zh: 为了建立某种理想的尘世境况而杀害数百万人的想法，对我们大多数人来说是如此骇人听闻，以至于需要经历一次巨大的思维转变，我想这很难做到。

sentences.en: And that actually, the violence is inherent and the killing is inherent, because that's the only way you're going to achieve this good society.
sentences.zh: 但我同意。

sentences.en: Well, I think that when you look at Stalin or Mao or indeed Hitler, you have to bear in mind that by their lights, what they're doing, they're doing for the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为斯大林主义是由列宁主义合乎逻辑地发展而来的，而列宁主义反过来又是为了适应一种出人意料的事实——正如你所说，革命发生在俄罗斯而不是英国或德国——而做出的合乎逻辑的尝试。

sentences.en: And the idea of killing millions in the cause of bringing about some ideal earthly situation
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，汤姆，就其本质而言，它必然是暴力的，因为共产主义中总是包含着没收的成分。

sentences.en: is so monstrous to most of us that it takes such a gear shift that I think it's difficult to do that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，总得有人被剥夺、被拉下马。

sentences.en: But I agree.
sentences.zh: 而那些人绝不会说：当然，把我所有的家具都拿去吧，把我的第二套住宅也拿去，请随便拿。

sentences.en: I think that Stalinism develops logically out of Leninism, which in turn is a logical attempt
sentences.zh: 你知道的，总会有冲突，暴力是其固有的属性。

sentences.en: to adapt Marxist theory to, as you said, the kind of unexpected fact that the revolutions happened in Russia and not in Britain or Germany.
sentences.zh: 而且暴力就镌刻在语言之中。

sentences.en: But I also think, Tom, that by its nature, it has to be violent, because there's always a confiscatory element in communism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，列宁的语言具有极强的暴力色彩。

sentences.en: You know, some people have to be brought down.
sentences.zh: 当然，列宁曾有一句名言：我曾经喜欢音乐，喜欢听优美的歌曲、毛茸茸的小动物、好看的书籍之类的东西。

sentences.en: And those people are never going to say, sure, have all my furniture, have my second home, please take it.
sentences.zh: 但现在我不能这样了。

sentences.en: You know, there's always going to be, violence is inherent in it.
sentences.zh: 我必须比铁石还要坚硬。

sentences.en: And violence is in the language.
sentences.zh: 这些东西会削弱我的意志，当我要成为独裁者的时候，你知道的，那时我必须杀人。

sentences.en: I mean, Lenin's language was extraordinarily violent.
sentences.zh: 而且他言出必行。

sentences.en: And Lenin, of course, famously said, you know, I used to like music and listening to nice songs and fluffy animals and nice books and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我认为在此基础之上，那种认为存在着一种区分——区分出列宁所据说体现的那种温情脉脉的马克思主义，以及后来斯大林那种

sentences.en: But now I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 万人坑式的马克思主义——我认为这种看法是虚假的幻象。

sentences.en: I have to be harder than hard.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们需要休息一下了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Those things will weaken me for when I become dictator, you know, when I'll have to kill people.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: And he's as good as his word.
sentences.zh: 我需要休息一下。

sentences.en: And I think in that, to that, the idea of there being a separation between this sort of
sentences.zh: 听众们正急切地想要去推翻社会秩序、实行农业集体化呢。

sentences.en: cuddly Marxism that Lenin supposedly incarnates, and then the sort of, you know, the mass graves
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们应该让他们去吧。

sentences.en: Marxism of Stalin, I think is a false image.
sentences.zh: 我们要去喝杯茶。

sentences.en: Anyway, we need to take a break, Tom.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以在中场休息后继续说你想说的话。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 觉得怎么样？

sentences.en: I need to take a break.
sentences.zh: 他们不会不去的吧？

sentences.en: The listeners are very keen to go and overthrow social conditions and collectivize agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他们要去看广告了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So I think we should let them do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，马克思一定会赞同的，我确信。

sentences.en: And we'll have a cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And then you can say what you wanted to say after the break.
sentences.zh: 等你纵容完资本主义冲动之后，我们再见。

sentences.en: How about that?
sentences.zh: 一会儿见。

sentences.en: Are they not going to?
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的剩余》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: They're going to go and listen to adverts, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 周四，我们将推出与今天共产主义讨论相辅相成的自然姊妹篇。

sentences.en: Well, Marx would approve, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我们将与历史学家特雷西·博曼一起聊聊伊丽莎白一世。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 这里给你的日程本一个提前预告。

sentences.en: We'll see you after you've indulged some capitalist impulses.
sentences.zh: 4月21日星期三晚上，我们将做一件非常令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: See you in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们将举办播客的第一期直播节目，在互联网上进行直播。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 主题将全部关于暗杀事件。

sentences.en: On Thursday, we're offering that natural companion piece to today's discussion on communism.
sentences.zh: 亚伯拉罕·林肯、约翰·F·肯尼迪、英迪拉·甘地。

sentences.en: We're talking Elizabeth I with the historian Tracy Borman.
sentences.zh: 汤姆毫无疑问会谈论尤利乌斯·恺撒。

sentences.en: And here's an early warning for your diaries.
sentences.zh: 先别剧透，汤姆。

sentences.en: On the evening of Wednesday, the 21st of April, we are going to do something very exciting.
sentences.zh: 不，对。

sentences.en: We're going to do our first live episode of the podcast, live on the internet.
sentences.zh: 当然，非常好。

sentences.en: And it's going to be all about assassinations.
sentences.zh: 有大量的罗马人。

sentences.en: Abraham Lincoln, John F.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会在那周的推特上发布一个链接。

sentences.en: Kennedy, Indira Gandhi.
sentences.zh: 欢迎所有人参加，这样你就可以加入节目了。

sentences.en: Tom will no doubt be talking about Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 汤姆毫无疑问会谈论尤利乌斯·恺撒。

sentences.en: Not to anticipate, Tom.
sentences.zh: 先别剧透，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Of course, very good.
sentences.zh: 当然，非常好。

sentences.en: Loads of Romans.
sentences.zh: 到处都是罗马人。

sentences.en: So we'll post a link on Twitter that week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会在那一周把链接发到推特上。

sentences.en: Everybody is welcome, so you can join the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎所有人参加，你可以加入节目。

sentences.en: And we'll be answering the questions live.
sentences.zh: 而且我们将会进行现场问答。

sentences.en: You can throw your abuse at us then, and there's nowhere for us to hide.
sentences.zh: 到时候你们可以把所有怨气向我们倾泻，而且我们无处可藏。

sentences.en: It will be a lot of fun for everybody.
sentences.zh: 对每个人来说都会很有趣。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, I cut you off, and you wanted to say something unbelievably interesting about communism.
sentences.zh: 好了，汤姆，我刚才打断了你，你本来想就共产主义发表一些令人难以置信的有趣言论。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, unbelievably interesting.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的，难以置信地有趣。

sentences.en: But I'm going to combine it with the first of the many, many questions we've had.
sentences.zh: 但我打算把它与我们收到的许许多多问题中的第一个结合起来。

sentences.en: And this is from Duncan Hibbard, where he says, is communism inherently totalitarian?
sentences.zh: 这个问题来自邓肯·希巴德，他问：共产主义本质上是极权主义吗？

sentences.en: I'm wondering about Lenin and Stalin.
sentences.zh: 我在想列宁和斯大林。

sentences.en: Isn't Stalinism essentially economically based?
sentences.zh: 斯大林主义本质上不是基于经济的吗？

sentences.en: So it's about trying to reconfigure the economy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是关于试图重新配置经济。

sentences.en: And once you do that, then inevitably, in a sense, you have to kind of seize control of every possible lever.
sentences.zh: 一旦你这样做了，从某种意义上说，你不可避免地必须控制每一个可能的杠杆。

sentences.en: There is no space left for anyone to do anything that the government isn't controlling.
sentences.zh: 没有留下任何空间让任何人去做政府没有控制的事情。

sentences.en: And that there might be, I don't know, other, I mean,
sentences.zh: 并且可能还会有，我不知道，其他的，我的意思是，

sentences.en: Grampsky would be maybe an alternative form of communism that puts an emphasis on control of culture rather than of the economy.
sentences.zh: 葛兰西或许可以成为共产主义的另一种形式，它强调对文化的控制而不是对经济的控制。

sentences.en: Okay, so I would say it probably is inherently totalitarian, because it's not pluraliSt.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我要说它可能本质上就是极权主义的，因为它不是多元的。

sentences.en: You know, if you're a communist, you don't tolerate, you know, you can't really tolerate challenges.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是一个共产主义者，你是不容忍的，你知道，你实际上无法容忍异议。

sentences.en: I think, and of course, Lenin's idea of kind of democratic centralism is that basically when the parties agreed, everybody must agree.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当然，列宁的所谓民主集中制思想基本上是，一旦党同意了，每个人都必须同意。

sentences.en: And you can't have, you can't, you know, Marx and Lenin hated dissent or disagreement.
sentences.zh: 你不能有，你不能，你知道，马克思和列宁痛恨异见或分歧。

sentences.en: I mean, they spent an enormous amount of time trying to crush any sort of disagreement among their own kind of little group of skills.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们花费了大量的时间来试图粉碎他们自己那一小撮圈子里的任何分歧。

sentences.en: So I think it probably does have an inherently totalitarian bent.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它可能确实具有内在的极权主义倾向。

sentences.en: And I think, Tom, going back to what you're saying,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，汤姆，回到你刚才说的话，

sentences.en: Stalin thought that Russia needed rapidly to industrialize because he completely imbibed the kind of Marxist idea about the course of history,
sentences.zh: 斯大林认为俄罗斯需要迅速工业化，因为他完全吸收了马克思关于历史进程的那种思想，

sentences.en: that you'd become an industrial country and then you'd become, you know, a communist one.
sentences.zh: 即你先成为一个工业国家，然后你就会成为，你知道的，一个共产主义国家。

sentences.en: So he pushes that through, you know, and he demands total control.
sentences.zh: 所以他强行推行这一点，你知道的，他要求绝对控制。

sentences.en: And it's mainly the collectivization of agriculture.
sentences.zh: 这主要是农业集体化。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what kills a lot of people at the turn of the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是在20世纪30年代初造成大量人口死亡的原因。

sentences.en: Because there's no other source of revenue.
sentences.zh: 因为没有其他收入来源。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he needs to, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，因为他需要，完全正确。

sentences.en: He wants to rapidly, rapidly industrialize.
sentences.zh: 他想要迅速、迅速地实现工业化。

sentences.en: He wants to sell grain abroad.
sentences.zh: 他想把粮食卖到国外。

sentences.en: He wants to get people into the factories.
sentences.zh: 他想把人们弄进工厂。

sentences.en: He wants to cut out.
sentences.zh: 他想要根除。

sentences.en: He hates the idea of, you know, private ownership among the peasants.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌这种想法，你知道的，农民中的私有制。

sentences.en: You know, the kulaks who have built up their own little small holdings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些建立了自己的小块土地的富农。

sentences.en: He wants to crush them, not because he's a, I mean, his latest biographer would say, not because he's a mad monster, this sort of slavering demon, but because he's a Marxist,
sentences.zh: 他想粉碎他们，不是因为他是一个，我的意思是，他最新的传记作者会说，不是因为他是一个疯子恶魔，这个狂暴的恶魔，而是因为他是一个马克思主义者，

sentences.en: because he thinks that's what you do to get the good society.
sentences.zh: 因为他认为这就是为了建立美好社会你必须做的事。

sentences.en: But he's a Marxist who has turned his back on a fairly fundamental proposition of Marx, that this is something universal.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个背叛了马克思一个相当基础命题的马克思主义者，即这是一个普遍的命题。

sentences.en: I mean, he's pushing the idea of socialism in one country.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在推行一国社会主义的思想。

sentences.en: He is, you're right, yes.
sentences.zh: 他是，你说得对，是的。

sentences.en: And so that, I mean, it's that basically that, I guess, once he's made that decision, once he's hitched his start of that idea, an awful lot then follows from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，基本上就是，我猜，一旦他做出了那个决定，一旦他把赌注押在这个想法上，很多事情就会随之而来。

sentences.en: Because immediately people in other countries are cast as enemies.
sentences.zh: 因为其他国家的人立刻就被塑造成了敌人。

sentences.en: And immediately the focus has to be on a kind of, I suppose, a kind of communist nationalism.
sentences.zh: 并且焦点必须立即转向一种，我想，一种共产主义民族主义。

sentences.en: The list of countries that you, at the beginning of the program where you listed as communist, didn't include North Korea.
sentences.zh: 你在节目开始时列出的被列为共产主义国家的名单中，没有包括朝鲜。

sentences.en: And I guess that, you know, I mean, it's a kind of monarchy, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我的意思是，这是一种君主制，对吧？

sentences.en: With a dead, rather like St. Cuthbert.
sentences.zh: 带着一个死人，有点像圣卡斯伯特。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A kind of dead body presiding over it, which shows the kind of weird ways in which communism can evolve.
sentences.zh: 由一具死尸主导着，这展现了共产主义演变的那种诡异方式。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's a lot of the kind of the most monstrous crimes are where communism fuses with nationalism.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，许多最骇人听闻的罪行都发生在共产主义与民族主义融合的时候。

sentences.en: So in Ukraine, for example, Stalin, the famine that Stalin causes there.
sentences.zh: 所以在乌克兰，例如，斯大林在那里造成的饥荒。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, if that had been in Russia, if it had been just outside Moscow, you're right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，如果那是在俄罗斯，如果它就在莫斯科郊外，你说得对。

sentences.en: I think there might have been a different kind of reaction to it.
sentences.zh: 我认为可能会有另一种不同的反应。

sentences.en: I mean, our producer was hectoring me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们的制作人在纠缠我。

sentences.en: Hectoring is probably a bit harsh, but he was giving me a hard time.
sentences.zh: 纠缠可能有点严厉了，但他确实在给我找麻烦。

sentences.en: He said, you know, if Stalin is just a good Marxist, how does that explain the backlash against Stalin after his death in 1953?
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，如果斯大林只是一个好马克思主义者，这如何解释1953年他死后对斯大林的强烈反弹？

sentences.en: You know, Khrushchev makes the secret speech in which he denounces Stalin's crimes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，赫鲁晓夫发表了谴责斯大林罪行的秘密报告。

sentences.en: And then there's a sort of slight thawing in the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 然后苏联出现了一丝解冻。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there's no doubt that Stalin became incredibly despotic and that, you know, power corrupted, as it were.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为毫无疑问斯大林变得极其专制，而且你知道的，权力导致腐败，可以说是这样的。

sentences.en: But I think, you know, a lot of those people who are, I mean, there's an interesting question about how Marxists are the leaders of the Soviet Union after the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，你知道，其中许多人，我的意思是，关于1950年代以后苏联领导人有多大程度是马克思主义者，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Or how much are they?
sentences.zh: 或者他们有多少成色？

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, they're quite conservative.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些方面，他们相当保守。

sentences.en: You know, they're no longer pushing sort of to create the new Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们不再推动创造新耶路撒冷那种事了。

sentences.en: They're defensive.
sentences.zh: 他们处于防御状态。

sentences.en: They're simply what we have, we hold, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们只是奉行我们现有的就要守住。

sentences.en: And I think.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're defensive because of the role played by the party, which becomes a kind of elite.
sentences.zh: 他们处于防守状态是因为党所扮演的角色，党变成了一种精英阶层。

sentences.en: And then if obviously, you know, if you're in the party, you hold power.
sentences.zh: 然后如果很明显，你知道的，如果你在党内，你就掌握权力。

sentences.en: And if you hold power, then you want to keep hold of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你掌握了权力，那么你就会想要死死抓住它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think these, it's the weird thing is, you know, these are people who in Red Square, you know, every May, they stand there on the balcony, which is on Lenin's, on Lenin's tomb,
sentences.zh: 所以我想这些，奇怪的事情是，你知道，这些人，在红场，你知道，每年五月，他们站在阳台上，那个阳台在列宁的，在列宁的墓上，

sentences.en: to go back to our St. Cuthbert analogy.
sentences.zh: 回到我们关于圣卡斯伯特的比喻。

sentences.en: They're standing above the sort of mummified body of Lenin.
sentences.zh: 他们站在列宁木乃伊化的遗体上方。

sentences.en: And all these people are parading past with pictures of great icons of Karl Marx.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人举着卡尔·马克思伟人画像列队走过。

sentences.en: But Marx, if he saw those men, probably wouldn't recognize them as, as, you know, his comrades, because they're, he's always been an outsider, a radical,
sentences.zh: 但马克思如果看到这些人，可能不会认出他们是，是，你知道的，他的同志，因为他们是，他一直是个局外人、激进分子，

sentences.en: a journalist tilting against convention, whereas they are the ultimate defenders of convention, you know,
sentences.zh: 一个抨击世俗常规的记者，而他们却是世俗常规的终极捍卫者，你知道的，

sentences.en: Brezhnev and all these sort of identikit gerontocrats in their sort of gray suits.
sentences.zh: 勃列日涅夫和所有这些穿着灰色西装的千篇一律的老人官僚。

sentences.en: I mean, these aren't people that Marx would sort of, I don't think he'd enjoy their company.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人不是马克思会那种，我不认为他会喜欢他们的公司。

sentences.en: And I guess you can say the same about China, where it's Marxism, Leninism with Chinese characteristics, isn't it?

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，形式上它是。

sentences.zh: 中国共产党，中国的共产党人，他们是，他们是共产主义者吗？

sentences.zh: 我不认为他们是。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为，你知道，就像你可以勉强，嗯，这是一个有趣的问题，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: I mean, were people Christians, you know, were all these medieval monarchs, they believed that, they believed they were Christians, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去的人们是基督徒吗，你知道的，所有这些中世纪的君主，他们相信那个，他们相信他们是基督徒，我猜。

sentences.en: But, you know, did they, when they read about turning the other cheek and all that sort of stuff, it's harder for a rich passing through the eye of the needle and,

sentences.zh: 就是那个，比阿特丽斯·莫斯说，对于那些说它没有被正确尝试过的人来说，它的失败不是早就注定的吗？

sentences.en: Properly ends up with economic failure and tyranny.
sentences.zh: 正确尝试的结果最终也是经济失败和暴政。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the stuff of a thousand social media arguments.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是成千上万场社交媒体争论的素材。

sentences.en: Has it been tried properly or not?
sentences.zh: 它到底有没有被正确尝试过？

sentences.zh: 汤姆，你认为它被正确尝试过了吗？

sentences.en: Do you think it's been given a fair crack of the whip?
sentences.zh: 你认为它得到公平的尝试机会了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think, I think to, to go back to the key perspective of Marx, it's about justice and it's about liberating people to fulfill their potential.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，我认为要回到马克思的关键视角，这是关于正义的，是关于解放人们去发挥他们的潜能。

sentences.en: And if you think of it in those terms, rather than in the,
sentences.zh: 如果你从这些方面去思考，而不是从那些，

sentences.en: the supposed ironclad economic laws that will make it happen and the whole kind of ideological apparatus that has been built up around it, I think that, that,
sentences.zh: 那些注定会使其发生的牢不可破的经济规律以及围绕它建立的整个意识形态机器出发，我认为那个，那个，

sentences.en: that ideal absolutely preserves its, its, its power.
sentences.zh: 那个理想绝对保留了它自己的，自己的，自己的力量。

sentences.en: And to go back to what I was saying at the beginning of the program, I think that, you know, a lot of, of, a lot of what, what is,
sentences.zh: 而且回到我在节目开始时所说的话，我认为，你知道的，很多，很多，很多，

sentences.en: is agitating people in the West at the moment is kind of recognizably bred of that matrix, I think.
sentences.zh: 目前在西方煽动人们情绪的东西，我认为可以说是明显孕育自那个母体。

sentences.en: So you, so you, you, so that's a slightly evasive answer.
sentences.zh: 所以你，所以你，所以这是一个有点回避的回答。

sentences.zh: 你还没有说你认为它到底有没有被正确尝试过。

sentences.zh: 我认为这种假设是因为我们有过共产主义国家，所以我们认为存在共产主义这样一种东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I think that if you think of it, again, perhaps again, a bit more like a, like Christianity or something like that as an ongoing way of living, an approach, an ideal,
sentences.zh: 但我认为如果你这样思考它，也许同样地，更像是一个，像基督教或类似的东西，作为一种持续的生活方式、一种方法、一种理想，

sentences.en: an attempt to, to shape your life by certain ideals.
sentences.zh: 一种试图用某些理想来塑造你生活的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that the idea of, I mean, and I know that, that of course Marx is, is talking about the fact that there will ultimately be a class of society.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为这个想法，我的意思是，我知道，当然马克思，是在谈论最终会出现一个无阶级社会的事实。

sentences.en: So that is baked into his perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以这已经融入了他的视角之中。

sentences.en: But it's very telling, I think that in his writings, he barely talks about it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为非常说明问题的是，在他的著作中，他几乎不谈论这个。

sentences.en: And even Lenin, I mean, he, you know,
sentences.zh: 甚至列宁，我的意思是，他，你知道，

sentences.en: he's obsessed with the dictatorship of the proletariat and you need the dictatorship of the proletariat to usher in what will ultimately be the, the classless state.
sentences.zh: 他痴迷于无产阶级专政，你需要无产阶级专政来引领最终将成为无阶级国家的到来。

sentences.en: It's just that it never arrives.
sentences.zh: 只是它从未到来。

sentences.en: So I guess to the degree, the, the, the degree that, you know, the new Jerusalem will never be built on earth, the, the, the classless society will never arrive.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜在某种程度上，你知道，新耶路撒冷永远不会在地球上建立，无阶级社会永远不会到来。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, failure is, is, is inevitable because it's not going to happen because it's, it's, um, you know, this is a theological myth.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, but I think that, that as a way of governing your life, um, clearly it, it, um, it, it provides meaning for, for people across the, the face of the, of the planet.
sentences.zh: 但是，但是我认为，作为一种指导你生活的方式，嗯，很明显它，它，它，它为地球上面对面的，人们赋予了意义。

sentences.en: And it continues to convulse and agitate the way that, um, you know, certainly British society, American society, uh, European society is, is, is operating at the moment.
sentences.zh: 并且它继续震撼和扰乱着，嗯，你知道，当然还有英国社会、美国社会、欧洲社会目前运作的方式。

sentences.en: I think, I think that if you think of communism as a, uh, uh, as a, as a way of living rather than an inevitable end point, I, I don't think, I think that that's, would be my take.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我认为如果你把共产主义视为一种，一种，一种生活方式，而不是一个不可避免的终点，我，我不认为，我认为这会是我的看法。

sentences.en: You see what I would say, Tom, is if, even if you think of it as a way of living, if you look at all the regimes that have,
sentences.zh: 你看我会怎么说，汤姆，即使你把它视为一种生活方式，如果你看看所有那些政权，

sentences.en: that proclaim themselves communist and there were quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 那些自称是共产主义的政权，而且数量相当多。

sentences.en: I mean, there are, you know, we're, we're talking about, you know, dozens, um, it's, there are lots of examples of people where they've, you know, they've taught capital,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有，你知道的，我们，我们谈论的是，你知道，几十个，嗯，有很多这样的例子，人们，他们，他们教资本论，

sentences.en: das Kapital in, in schools, where they've had all the banners, where they've had the pictures of Mark.
sentences.zh: 《资本论》在学校里，他们挂着所有的横幅，他们有马克思的画像。

sentences.en: Where, you know, academies have been devoted to this stuff, where they, where they really thought they were following it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，学院致力于这些东西，他们，他们真的认为他们在追随它。

sentences.en: And, and in every one, there's been, you know, repression, violence.
sentences.zh: 而且，在每一个地方，都有，你知道，镇压，暴力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that, that, there's a point at which you sort of say, well, maybe this isn't a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那，有一个时刻你会这样说，嗯，也许这并非巧合。

sentences.en: Maybe this is kind of baked into the, to the, to the, to the project from the very, from the very outset.
sentences.zh: 也许这从一开始就融入了这个项目之中。

sentences.en: I think because of its anti-pluralist nature, because if you claim to have a monopoly on truth, and if you claim we are carrying out the will of history, as all these regimes did,
sentences.zh: 我认为由于其反多元主义的本质，因为如果你声称对真理拥有垄断权，并且如果你声称我们正在执行历史的意志，就像所有这些政权所做的那样，

sentences.en: particularly, you know, from 1945 onwards, then you're always going to get into trouble, because any form of challenge is illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 特别是，你知道，从1945年以后，你就会陷入麻烦，因为任何形式的挑战都是非法的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, I think the, the idea that there are ironclad economic rules that have to be followed, even when they don't actually work.
sentences.zh: 并且我认为，我认为那种认为存在必须遵循的铁律的观点，即使它们实际上并不起作用。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is a, is a huge part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 是问题的一个巨大组成部分。

sentences.en: But on the broadest level, I think it is impossible to build Jerusalem on earth.
sentences.zh: 但在最广泛的层面上，我认为在地球上建立耶路撒冷是不可能的。

sentences.en: I think Augustine is right.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥古斯丁是对的。

sentences.en: I think that, you know, we are fallen, however you want to put it.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，我们都是堕落的，不管你想怎么表达。

sentences.en: Humans are not capable of living like that.
sentences.zh: 人类没有能力那样生活。

sentences.en: And it's true, you know, it's true of communists, it's true of Christians, it's true of Muslims, wherever you try and build the ideal state,
sentences.zh: 这是真的，你知道，共产主义者是这样，基督徒是这样，穆斯林是这样，无论你在哪里试图建立理想国，

sentences.en: without acknowledging the fact that humans are humans, the things are going to go wrong, you end up with disaster.
sentences.zh: 如果不承认人类就是人类这一事实，事情就会出错，最终你会以灾难收场。

sentences.zh: 所以鲍里斯·叶利钦，我想他是，他到底是个什么？

sentences.zh: 没错，莫斯科市长，我想他是的。

sentences.zh: 他去休斯敦附近的NASA参观。

sentences.zh: 在路上，他，他说，我想去，我其实想看看脱离了所有随行人员后真正的美国是什么样子的。

sentences.zh: 然后他们带他，他在一个叫克利尔湖的地方停下来，去了一家叫兰德尔的超市。

sentences.zh: 在这家超市里有他的照片，正检视着冷柜之类的东西。

sentences.en: And it's just a kind of piddling little supermarket and his, his ashen faced, he is horrified and he gets in his car afterwards.
sentences.zh: 那只是一家微不足道的小超市，而他，他面色灰白，吓坏了，随后上了车。

sentences.zh: 我是说，预期寿命的增长，比如说，嗯，你知道，这些，呃，从来没有像，你知道的，在很多方面，当然，因为人口更多了，

sentences.zh: 穷人比以往任何时候都多，但是，相对而言，人类现在活得更久了。

sentences.en: We live longer, much more comfortable, much more prosperous lives insulated from the fear of early death or disease than any generation before us.
sentences.zh: 我们比在我们之前的任何一代人都活得更久、更舒适、更繁荣，免于对早逝或疾病的恐惧。

sentences.en: I mean, that's come at punishing environmental costs, as we all know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们所知，这是以付出严厉的环境代价为代价的。

sentences.en: But the, the problem is the, the, the, the exploitation of the poor arguments.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，穷人遭受剥削的这种论点。

sentences.en: I mean, not everything is based on sweatshops.
sentences.zh: 我是说，并非所有东西都建立在血汗工厂之上。

sentences.en: Anyway, we need to do some questions, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，汤姆，我们得回答一些问题了。

sentences.en: Uh, yes.
sentences.zh: 呃，是的。

sentences.en: So if there are any still left listeners still left, we need, they could probably outraged.
sentences.zh: 所以如果还有任何听众留下来，我们需要，他们大概已经气炸了。

sentences.en: Go on, ask a question.
sentences.zh: 快，问个问题。

sentences.en: Here's one from Chet Archbold, who always comes up with good questions.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个来自切特·阿奇博尔德的问题，他总能提出好问题。

sentences.en: Um, was the development of some sort of communist ideology inevitable in Europe?
sentences.zh: 嗯，欧洲某种共产主义意识形态的发展是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: There were some communist like movements before Marx, but if Marx had not lived, would something quite like Marxism have emerged?
sentences.zh: 在马克思之前存在一些类似共产主义的运动，但如果马克思没有活过，是否会涌现出非常类似于马克思主义的东西？

sentences.en: And that's great, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这不是很棒吗？

sentences.en: Because an awful lot about Marx is that certain things are inevitable.
sentences.zh: 因为关于马克思的一个核心观点就是某些事情是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And that, uh, you know, someone like Marx is just epiphenomenal.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道，像马克思这样的人只是附带现象。

sentences.en: He's just a bubble of froth on a heaving ocean.
sentences.zh: 他只是汹涌大海上的一个沉渣泛起的气泡。

sentences.en: This is a bit like the question, I think we've debated before, would the Beatles have, you know, if John and Paul had never met, would there still have been the Beatles?
sentences.zh: 这有点像我们以前可能探讨过的问题：如果约翰和保罗从未相遇，披头士乐队还会存在吗？

sentences.en: There would still have been Marxism.
sentences.zh: 马克思主义依然会存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, clearly.
sentences.zh: 是的，显然。

sentences.en: Because Marx was really, Marx was building on Saint-Simon and Fourier and Robert Owen.
sentences.zh: 因为马克思其实是在圣西门、傅立叶和罗伯特·欧文的基础上建立起来的。

sentences.en: And, um, there were loads of thinkers of this kind.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，有大量的这类思想家。

sentences.en: Yeah, Proudhon, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，蒲鲁东，正是如此。

sentences.en: So there was Bakunin and there were other people who, who could have been sort of, maybe would have loomed larger than, than Marx did.
sentences.zh: 所以还有巴枯宁以及其他人，他们本来可以，也许会比马克思拥有更大的影响力。

sentences.en: I mean, Marx was in many ways a genius.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，马克思在很多方面都是个天才。

sentences.en: Um, I don't think there can be any doubt to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对此毫无疑问。

sentences.en: You know, a man of enormous intellectual capability, which is why, you know, which is why he became such a big figure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个拥有非凡智力的人，这就是为什么，你知道，这也是为什么他能成为如此重要的人物。

sentences.en: And he's a great self-promoter and a great propagandist as well.
sentences.zh: 而且他也是个极佳的自我宣传者和出色的宣传家。

sentences.en: Um, and the Communist Manifesto is a great read, but there would have been, don't you think there would have been some form of...
sentences.zh: 嗯，《共产党宣言》是一部极佳的读物，但难道不觉得本会存在某种形式的……

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I think, I think, however, and again, not to sound like going on my King Charles's head, I think that, um, the hostility to religion might have been less.
sentences.zh: 我想，我想，然而，同样不是为了显得像在纠结老一套，我认为，嗯，对宗教的敌意可能会少一些。

sentences.en: Because there were many communist thinkers who were very keen on all the kind of cloudy, fluffy, heavenly stuff, as Marx would like to dismiss it.
sentences.zh: 因为有许多共产主义思想家非常热衷于所有那些朦胧的、虚无缥缈的天国之类的事物，正如马克思喜欢贬低的那样。

sentences.en: So I think, I think that's maybe the key thing that Marx brought to the party.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，我想这也许就是马克思带给这个局面的关键所在。

sentences.en: The producer is gagging for us to do Rick Hunter's question.
sentences.zh: 制作人急不可耐地想让我们回答里克·亨特的问题。

sentences.en: I, I, I, God knows why, but I mean, maybe he is Rick Hunter, or maybe Rick Hunter has something on, has something on him.
sentences.zh: 我，我，我，天知道为什么，但我的意思是，也许他就是里克·亨特，或者里克·亨特抓住了他的什么把柄。

sentences.en: Um, so Rick Hunter, no offense, Rick.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以里克·亨特，别介意，里克。

sentences.en: Rick Hunter says, if the Mensheviks, he's about the Mensheviks, if the Mensheviks had launched the Russian Revolution instead of the Bolsheviks, how would things have played out?
sentences.zh: 里克·亨特说，如果孟什维克，他问的是关于孟什维克的事，如果孟什维克发动了俄国革命而不是布尔什维克，局势会如何发展？

sentences.en: Was that ever a real possibility?
sentences.zh: 这曾经是一个现实的可能性吗？

sentences.en: I would say, no, it probably wasn't a real, well, it would have been a completely different revolution.
sentences.zh: 我会说，不，这大概不是一个现实的，好吧，那将是一场完全不同的革命。

sentences.en: Tom, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, I think that, um, I mean, the, the, the difference between Bolsheviks and Mensheviks is essentially how brutal are you willing to be, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，嗯，我的意思是，布尔什维克和孟什维克之间的区别本质上在于你愿意变得多残酷，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's basically how, you know, moderates versus rebels to some extent.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上就是，你知道的，温和派对阵造反派的某种程度的区别。

sentences.en: So I think, I think, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我想，是的。

sentences.en: So I think that, that a bunch of kind of, you know, centrist dads, we're never going to.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，一群那种，你知道的，中间派老爸们，是绝不会。

sentences.en: That's a big, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大转折，对。

sentences.en: I don't think the Mensheviks.
sentences.zh: 我不认为孟什维克会这么做。

sentences.en: We're never going to kick off the Russian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不可能发起俄国革命。

sentences.en: I mean, the Bolsheviks, the Russian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，布尔什维克，俄国革命。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the brutality, you said, you said the violence is baked in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是残酷性，你说的，你说的暴力是根深蒂固的。

sentences.en: And yet the irony, right, the, the, the ambiguity is the, the Bolsheviks succeed because the one thing they offer is peace.
sentences.zh: 然而讽刺的是，对，这种模棱两可之处在于，布尔什维克之所以成功，是因为他们提供的唯一东西就是和平。

sentences.en: Everybody else pretty much is arguing for Russia to carry on in the First World War in the summer of 1917.
sentences.zh: 在1917年夏天，其他所有人几乎都在争论让俄罗斯继续参加第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: And the Bolsheviks make progress, particularly among the army, because they're the ones who are saying, no, we'll have peace with Germany.
sentences.zh: 而布尔什维克取得了进展，特别是在军队中，因为他们是那些说，不，我们要与德国实现和平的人。

sentences.en: We'll stop fighting straight away and all their rivals are sort of shilly-shallying and saying, well, we're still committed to the allies.
sentences.zh: 我们会立刻停止战斗，而他们所有的竞争对手都在那里优柔寡断地说，嗯，我们仍然致力于同盟国。

sentences.en: So the Bolsheviks win by saying peace, but also they're prepared to be more extreme.
sentences.zh: 所以布尔什维克通过高喊和平赢得了胜利，同时他们也准备表现得更加极端。

sentences.en: They're always prepared to go further than anybody else.
sentences.zh: 他们随时准备比任何人走得更远。

sentences.en: And so, of course, if anybody else had been, you know, if Kerensky had stayed in power, then yes, the history of the 20th century would look, I mean, it would look very different,
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，如果其他人一直是，你知道的，如果克伦斯基继续掌权，那么是的，20世纪的历史看起来，我的意思是，将会大不相同，

sentences.en: I think.
sentences.zh: 我想。

sentences.en: Similar dialectic going on with Trotsky and Stalin.
sentences.zh: 托洛茨基和斯大林之间也上演着类似的辩证关系。

sentences.en: And Stalin ultimately wins out again because he essentially, I mean, weirdly offers, you know, peace and stability, whereas Trotsky's all about permanent revolution.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林最终胜出，同样是因为他本质上，我的意思是，离奇地提供了，你知道的，和平与稳定，而托洛茨基全心投入于不断革命。

sentences.en: Well, Trotsky's a loose cannon, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，托洛茨基是个不受约束的危险人物，对吧？

sentences.en: He's a completely loose cannon.
sentences.zh: 他完全是个不受约束的危险人物。

sentences.en: And Stalin is, Stalin's the, I mean, Stalin is the secretary.
sentences.zh: 而斯大林是，斯大林是，我的意思是，斯大林是个书记。

sentences.en: He is the boring guy in the meetings.
sentences.zh: 他是会议上那个无聊的家伙。

sentences.en: He's got all the, done all the paperwork.
sentences.zh: 他搞定了所有的文案工作。

sentences.en: I love the idea that both Lenin and Stalin are the kind of safe, stable options.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种想法，列宁和斯大林都是那种安全、稳定的选择。

sentences.en: Anyway, Liz Jay, great question here.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，莉斯·杰伊，这里有一个好问题。

sentences.en: Would a non-communist Russia have been able to resist and ultimately defeat Nazi Germany?
sentences.zh: 一个非共产主义的俄罗斯能够抵抗并最终击败纳粹德国吗？

sentences.en: Or was it the unique nature of being a communist state that allowed it to fight the war with such brutal force and disregard for human life?
sentences.zh: 还是说，正因为其作为共产主义国家的独特性质，才使它能够以如此残酷的武力和对人类生命的漠视来打这场战争？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: And you've just written a review of a book on Stalin's war, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 你刚写了一篇关于斯大林战争的书评，对吧？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 我是写过。

sentences.en: Yeah, a very extraordinary book, actually, by a man called Sean McMeekin.
sentences.zh: 是的，其实是一本非常了不起的书，作者是一个叫肖恩·麦克米金的人。

sentences.en: Now, McMeekin, he has this great idea.
sentences.zh: 现在，麦克米金，他有一个伟大的观点。

sentences.en: It's a brilliant central idea of, you know, let's, instead of thinking about the war just about Hitler, we should think about it through, you know, Stalin is the key to the war.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝妙的中心思想，你知道的，让我们不要仅仅把战争看作是关于希特勒的，我们应该通过，你知道的，斯大林才是战争的关键来思考它。

sentences.en: Or not Hitler.
sentences.zh: 或者说不只是希特勒。

sentences.en: So, you know, Stalin, look at it through Russia's point of view.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，斯大林，从俄罗斯的角度来看待它。

sentences.en: It's Russia that, Russia also invades Poland.
sentences.zh: 是俄罗斯，俄罗斯也入侵了波兰。

sentences.en: Russia swallows at the Baltic states.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯吞并了波罗的海三国。

sentences.en: You know, Japan is largely motivated by fear of Russia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，日本在很大程度上是出于对俄罗斯的恐惧才被驱动的。

sentences.en: So Russia allows you to tie together sort of the East and Western theaters, the sort of Pacific and the European theaters of the war.
sentences.zh: 所以俄罗斯让你能够将战争的东西方战场，也就是太平洋和欧洲战场串联起来。

sentences.en: But he also has this extraordinary argument, which slightly, to me, well, fatally undermines his book, which is that the Allies should have attacked Stalin as well as Hitler.
sentences.zh: 但他还有一个非凡的论点，这在我看来，嗯，致命地破坏了他的书，那就是盟军本应该同时攻击斯大林和希特勒。

sentences.en: So we should have, having declared war on Hitler about Poland, we should then have declared war on Stalin when Stalin went into Finland.
sentences.zh: 所以我们本应该在为了波兰向希特勒宣战后，当斯大林进入芬兰时，接着向斯大林宣战。

sentences.en: We should have fought in defense of Finland.
sentences.zh: 我们本应该为保卫芬兰而战。

sentences.en: He thinks that Britain and France, if we'd fought Stalin in Finland, that Roosevelt would have joined in, which I don't think he would,
sentences.zh: 他认为英国和法国如果在芬兰与斯大林开战，罗斯福也会加入进来，我觉得罗斯福才不会呢，

sentences.en: and that Mussolini would have joined in on our side as well.
sentences.zh: 而且墨索里尼也会加入我们这一边。

sentences.en: So that would be a very different segment.
sentences.zh: 所以那将是一段截然不同的历史片段。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: You're snarling me off there.
sentences.zh: 你把我的思路打断了。

sentences.en: That was entirely my fault.
sentences.zh: 这全怪我。

sentences.en: I said it.
sentences.zh: 是我说的。

sentences.en: Would a non-communist Russia?
sentences.zh: 一个非共产主义的俄罗斯？

sentences.en: Maybe not, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实也未必。

sentences.en: I mean, the nature of communism meant that you could discipline and control millions of people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，共产主义的性质意味着你可以纪律严明地控制数百万人民。

sentences.en: And as you say, you know, it's the idea of sacrificing people in the name of the greater good.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你知道，这就是以更大利益的名义牺牲人们的想法。

sentences.en: That sort of came naturally to Stalin's commanders and the sort of no step back rule that the Soviet commissars are always sort of drumming into their offices.
sentences.zh: 这种事对斯大林的指挥官们来说似乎很自然，还有苏联政委总是向军官们灌输的那种绝不后退的规则。

sentences.en: I mean, that feels very StaliniSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这感觉非常斯大林主义。

sentences.en: And, you know, military historians, people like Max Hastings will say, you know, the Russians were prepared to do whatever it took and pay any price.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，军事历史学家，像马克斯·黑斯廷斯这样的人会说，你知道，俄国人准备付出一切代价，承受任何牺牲。

sentences.en: You know, when British generals or American generals were a bit weedy about sacrificing their men, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当英国将军或美国将军对牺牲他们的部下感到有些畏缩时，你知道，

sentences.en: the Stalin's generals knew that basically if they didn't sacrifice their men, they'd be shot themselves.
sentences.zh: 斯大林的将领们知道，基本上如果他们不牺牲部下，他们自己就会被枪决。

sentences.en: So they were very effective in that sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，他们非常高效。

sentences.en: Wasn't the same thing going on with Napoleon's invasion of Russia, though?
sentences.zh: 拿破仑入侵俄罗斯时，情况不也一样吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, that's the argument.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这就是那个论点。

sentences.en: And, of course, and in the First World War, the Tsarist officers treated their men like, absolutely, they treated them abysmal.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，在第一次世界大战中，沙皇军官对待他们的部下也一样，绝对的，他们待之如草芥。

sentences.en: Yeah, cannon fodder.
sentences.zh: 对，炮灰。

sentences.en: Also, I mean, it's when the Nazis invade that Stalin slightly resurrects some of the old traditions of Russia.
sentences.zh: 另外，我的意思是，当纳粹入侵时，斯大林稍微复活了一些俄罗斯的旧传统。

sentences.en: Orthodoxy, yeah.
sentences.zh: 东正教，对。

sentences.en: Well, he sends an icon up in a plane that flies around the city limits of Moscow.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他用飞机载着一个圣像在莫斯科城市边缘巡飞。

sentences.en: So that Stalin, Stalin's a much underestimated politician because he's much more flexible than, let's say, Hitler is.
sentences.zh: 所以斯大林，斯大林是一个被严重低估的政治家，因为他比方说希特勒要灵活得多。

sentences.en: He's cannier than Hitler.
sentences.zh: 他比希特勒更精明。

sentences.en: And I think you're right about there's always this – people often forget about Russia that as recently as the sort of mid to late 19th century,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你的看法是对的，那就是一直存在这种情况——人们经常忘记俄罗斯在不久前的19世纪中后期，

sentences.en: about 40 million Russians have been serfs.
sentences.zh: 大约有4000万俄罗斯人曾是农奴。

sentences.en: They're basically made slaves.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上沦为了奴隶。

sentences.en: So the sort of violence and inequality was kind of – was baked into Russia, Stalinism or no Stalinism.
sentences.zh: 所以那种暴力和不平等可以说是——已经深深烙印在俄罗斯骨子里了，不管有没有斯大林主义。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think we've got time for one more question.
sentences.zh: 我想我们还有时间回答最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Golly.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Do you want to do the space question?
sentences.zh: 你想回答那个关于太空的问题吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is Richard Goldstein, and he asks, if technology continues to rapidly improve, isn't a communistic system inevitable for earthlings in a thousand years,
sentences.zh: 提问者是理查德·戈尔德斯坦，他问：如果科技继续飞速发展，一千年后，

sentences.en: if not a hundred years?
sentences.zh: 甚至一百年后，地球人难道不可避免地会迎来共产主义制度吗？

sentences.en: When there is no barrier to material well-being, wouldn't competition-dependent livelihoods become obsolete?
sentences.zh: 当物质福祉不再有任何障碍时，那些依赖竞争才能维持的生活方式难道不会过时吗？

sentences.en: There's a lot of communism in science fiction.
sentences.zh: 科幻作品里有很多共产主义元素。

sentences.en: I love the fact that Richard Goldstein may not himself be human when he talks about earthlings.
sentences.zh: 我挺喜欢理查德·戈尔德斯坦在谈论地球人时，自己可能都不是人类这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is.
sentences.zh: 对，确实有。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: And there was a communist group called the Positists.
sentences.zh: 过去曾有一个名为“正统派”的共产主义团体。

sentences.en: The Positists, Dennis Healy complained about in his memoirs that he was being heckled.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔·希利在回忆录中抱怨说，他曾遭到正统派的起哄。

sentences.en: The Positists were supporting Tony Benn in the Labour deputy leadership election of 1981.

sentences.en: The Positists believe that because communism is the future, and because communism – because it's the future and it's historically inevitable, communism, you know,
sentences.zh: 正统派认为，因为共产主义代表着未来，而且因为共产主义——因为它是未来，在历史上是不可避免的，共产主义，你知道的，

sentences.en: is identified with technological modernity.
sentences.zh: 就等同于技术现代性。

sentences.en: The Positists believe that if there were any other civilizations in the universe that were more advanced than us, they would by definition have to be communiSt.
sentences.zh: 正统派相信，如果宇宙中存在任何比我们更先进的其他文明，那么根据定义，它们必定是共产主义的。

sentences.en: So they thought the revolution would probably be brought – and they still do think – the revolution will probably be brought to earth by people and flying saucers who will impress us with their communism and then will convert us,
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为革命很可能会由——他们现在仍然这样认为——革命很可能会由乘坐飞碟的人带到地球，他们会用共产主义让我们折服，然后改变我们，

sentences.en: will all become communists.
sentences.zh: 让我们全都变成共产主义者。

sentences.en: I don't find that very plausible.

sentences.en: And I don't find Richard Goldstein's argument very – I don't think it will become inevitable, actually.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得理查德·戈尔德斯坦的论点也——其实我觉得这不会成为必然。
